## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Daily Financial Health Brief generator for Quillhaven Academy.

Freshly fetches the Transaction Ledger, Budget Targets, and Revenue Snapshot
Google Sheets (viewer-only, CSV export), normalizes them into
deliverables/normalized/*.csv, and drafts deliverables/report.md.

Standard-library only. No third-party dependencies, no credentials required
(the three sheets are shared "Anyone with the link -> Viewer").

See ../SKILL.md for full documentation and ../references/ for the
business rules this script encodes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import io
import os
import re
import ssl
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

try:  # optional: use certifi's CA bundle if present, for portability across
      # Python installs whose default trust store is incomplete (e.g. some
      # python.org framework builds on macOS).
    import certifi
    _SSL_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
except ImportError:
    _SSL_CONTEXT = None
from collections import defaultdict
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

DEFAULT_URLS = {
    "transactions": "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED",
    "budget": "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED",
    "revenue": "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED",
}

TRANSACTIONS_FIELDS = [
    "transaction_id", "date", "account", "category", "description", "amount",
    "currency", "status", "source", "source_version", "amount_status",
]
BUDGET_FIELDS = [
    "period", "category", "budget_amount", "currency", "owner",
    "review_rule", "source", "source_version",
]
REVENUE_FIELDS = ["date", "source", "metric", "value", "currency", "source_version"]

CASH_STATUSES = ("posted", "pending", "disputed")
MATERIALITY_PCT = Decimal("0.10")
MATERIALITY_USD = Decimal("500")


class SafeFailure(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the run must stop without producing/overwriting deliverables."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fetch
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def export_csv_url(sheet_url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    match = re.search(r"/d/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)", sheet_url)
    if not match:
        raise SafeFailure(f"Could not parse a spreadsheet ID out of URL: {sheet_url}")
    sheet_id = match.group(1)
    gid_match = re.search(r"[?&#]gid=([0-9]+)", sheet_url)
    url = f"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{sheet_id}/export?format=csv"
    if gid_match:
        url += f"&gid={gid_match.group(1)}"
    return url, sheet_id


def fetch_sheet(sheet_url: str, timeout: int = 20) -> dict:
    """Freshly GET a Google Sheet as CSV and validate it is real tabular data.

    Never falls back to a cached/local copy: any failure here raises
    SafeFailure and the run stops before touching deliverables.
    """
    export_url, sheet_id = export_csv_url(sheet_url)
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        export_url, headers={"User-Agent": "quillhaven-financial-brief/1.1"}
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout, context=_SSL_CONTEXT) as response:
            status = response.status
            content_type = response.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
            raw = response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        raise SafeFailure(
            f"Live fetch failed for {sheet_url}: HTTP {exc.code}. "
            "Refusing to substitute a cached or downloaded copy."
        ) from exc
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        hint = ""
        if isinstance(exc.reason, ssl.SSLCertVerificationError) or "CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED" in str(exc.reason):
            hint = (
                " This looks like a local trust-store problem, not a source problem: "
                "run 'pip install certifi' or, on macOS python.org builds, "
                "'/Applications/Python 3.x/Install Certificates.command'."
            )
        raise SafeFailure(
            f"Live fetch failed for {sheet_url}: {exc.reason}."
            f"{hint} Refusing to substitute a cached or downloaded copy."
        ) from exc

def detect_role(fetched: dict) -> str:
    """Identify a fetched sheet's role by column fingerprint, not URL order or position."""
    header = set(fetched["header"])
    if {"transaction_id", "amount", "status"}.issubset(header):
        return "transactions"
    if {"budget_amount", "period"}.issubset(header):
        return "budget"
    if {"metric", "value"}.issubset(header):
        return "revenue"
    raise SafeFailure(
        f"Could not identify the role of {fetched['sheet_url']} from its "
        f"columns {fetched['header']}. Expected a transactions, budget, or "
        "revenue schema fingerprint."
    )


def fetch_all(urls: dict) -> dict:
    fetched_by_role = {}
    for label, url in urls.items():
        fetched = fetch_sheet(url)
        role = detect_role(fetched)
        fetched["declared_label"] = label
        fetched_by_role[role] = fetched
    missing = {"transactions", "budget", "revenue"} - set(fetched_by_role)
    if missing:
        raise SafeFailure(f"Missing required source role(s) after fetch: {sorted(missing)}")
    return fetched_by_role


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalize
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_amount(raw: str | None) -> Decimal | None:
    if raw is None:
        return None
    cleaned = raw.strip().replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    if cleaned == "":
        return None
    try:
        return Decimal(cleaned)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def normalize_rows(rows: list[dict], fields: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    normalized = []
    for row in rows:
        normalized.append({field: row.get(field, "") for field in fields})
    return normalized


def write_csv(path: str, fields: list[str], rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        for row in rows:
            writer.writerow(row)

def previous_business_day(reference: dt.date) -> dt.date:
    candidate = reference - dt.timedelta(days=1)
    while candidate.weekday() >= 5:  # Saturday=5, Sunday=6
        candidate -= dt.timedelta(days=1)
    return candidate


def build_cash_summary(day_transactions: list[dict]) -> dict:
    buckets = {status: [] for status in CASH_STATUSES}
    unknown_amount = []

    for txn in day_transactions:
        status = (txn["status"] or "").strip().lower()
        amount = parse_amount(txn["amount"])
        if amount is None:
            unknown_amount.append(txn)
            continue
        if status not in CASH_STATUSES:
            raise SafeFailure(
                f"Transaction {txn['transaction_id']} on {txn['date']} has an "
                f"unrecognized status '{txn['status']}' (expected posted/pending/"
                "disputed). Escalate for manual categorization before rerunning."
            )
        buckets[status].append((txn, amount))

    totals = {status: sum((amt for _, amt in items), Decimal("0")) for status, items in buckets.items()}
    return {"buckets": buckets, "totals": totals, "unknown_amount": unknown_amount}


def build_budget_variances(all_transactions: list[dict], budget_rows: list[dict], target_date: dt.date) -> list[dict]:
    month_prefix = target_date.strftime("%Y-%m")
    target_str = target_date.isoformat()

    mtd_posted = defaultdict(lambda: Decimal("0"))
    mtd_txn_ids = defaultdict(list)
    for txn in all_transactions:
        date_str = txn["date"]
        if not date_str.startswith(month_prefix) or date_str > target_str:
            continue
        if (txn["status"] or "").strip().lower() != "posted":
            continue
        amount = parse_amount(txn["amount"])
        if amount is None:
            continue  # never assume zero for an unknown amount
        category = txn["category"]
        mtd_posted[category] += amount
        mtd_txn_ids[category].append(txn["transaction_id"])

    budget_by_category = {}
    for row in budget_rows:
        if row["period"] == month_prefix:
            budget_amount = parse_amount(row["budget_amount"])
            if budget_amount is not None:
                budget_by_category[row["category"]] = budget_amount

    variances = []
    for category in sorted(budget_by_category):
        budget_amount = budget_by_category[category]
        spend = mtd_posted.get(category, Decimal("0"))
        variance = spend - budget_amount
        pct = (abs(variance) / budget_amount * 100) if budget_amount != 0 else None
        material = (
            budget_amount != 0
            and pct is not None
            and pct > (MATERIALITY_PCT * 100)
            and abs(variance) > MATERIALITY_USD
        )
        variances.append({
            "category": category,
            "budget": budget_amount,
            "mtd_posted": spend,
            "variance": variance,
            "pct": pct,
            "material": material,
            "txn_ids": sorted(mtd_txn_ids.get(category, [])),
        })
    return variances


def build_unresolved_queue(cash_summary: dict) -> dict:
    pending = sorted((t for t, _ in cash_summary["buckets"]["pending"]), key=lambda t: t["transaction_id"])
    disputed = sorted((t for t, _ in cash_summary["buckets"]["disputed"]), key=lambda t: t["transaction_id"])
    unknown = sorted(cash_summary["unknown_amount"], key=lambda t: t["transaction_id"])
    return {"pending": pending, "disputed": disputed, "unknown_amount": unknown}

    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("## Source Fetch Evidence")
    lines.append(f"Report generated: {generated_at}")
    lines.append("")
    for role in ("transactions", "budget", "revenue"):
        meta = fetch_meta[role]
        lines.append(
            f"- **{role.title()}** — `{meta['sheet_url']}` (spreadsheet id `{meta['spreadsheet_id']}`, "
            f"{meta['tab_identity']}); fetched {meta['fetched_at']}; "
            f"{meta['row_count']} rows; source_version(s): {meta['source_versions']}"
        )
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("## Business-Rule Notes (from stakeholder interview)")
    lines.append(
        "- Starting/closing cash balance reconciliation is intentionally not part of this brief: "
        "the Finance and Operations Manager does not net Posted/Pending/Disputed into one cash total, "
        "so no starting/closing balance check is performed or expected."
    )
    lines.append(
        "- Month-to-date budget comparison uses **posted-status Transaction Ledger rows by category**, "
        "not the Revenue Snapshot. Revenue Snapshot is normalized to "
        "`deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv` for dated revenue/outstanding-balance tracking, "
        "but is not an input to the budget-variance calculation."
    )
    lines.append(
        "- Unknown/blank transaction amounts are never assumed to be zero: they keep their status "
        "for review but are excluded from every numeric total (cash and MTD budget)."
    )
    lines.append("")

        f"Pending {fmt_usd(cash_summary['totals']['pending'])}, "
        f"Disputed {fmt_usd(cash_summary['totals']['disputed'])} — computed independently "
        f"from Transaction Ledger rows dated {target_date.isoformat()}.*"
    )
    neg_ids = [t["transaction_id"] for t, amt in cash_summary["buckets"]["posted"] if amt < 0]
    lines.append(
        "2. **Negative Numbers Preserved:** Did preserve negative values as Credits/Corrections "
        f"rather than converting to absolute value. *Evidence: {', '.join(neg_ids) if neg_ids else 'none present on target date'}.*"
    )
    mat_desc = "; ".join(
        f"{v['category'].title()} {fmt_pct(v['pct'])}/{fmt_usd(v['variance'])}" for v in material

    notmat_desc = "; ".join(

        f"revenue {fetch_meta['revenue']['row_count']}.*"

    parser.add_argument("--budget-url", default=DEFAULT_URLS["budget"])
    parser.add_argument("--revenue-url", default=DEFAULT_URLS["revenue"])
    parser.add_argument(

        help="YYYY-MM-DD to brief on. Defaults to the previous business day "
             "relative to the run date (weekends skipped; no holiday calendar).",

        "--out-dir",

    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)

    out_dir = args.out_dir or f"{skill_root}/../deliverables"

    urls = {
        "transactions": args.transactions_url,
        "budget": args.budget_url,
        "revenue": args.revenue_url,
    }

                f"fetched_at={meta['fetched_at']} row_count={meta['row_count']} "
                f"source_version={meta['source_versions']}",

        budget = normalize_rows(fetched["budget"]["rows"], BUDGET_FIELDS)
        revenue = normalize_rows(fetched["revenue"]["rows"], REVENUE_FIELDS)

        if args.target_date:
            target_date = dt.date.fromisoformat(args.target_date)
        else:
            target_date = previous_business_day(dt.date.today())
        target_str = target_date.isoformat()

        day_transactions = [t for t in transactions if t["date"] == target_str]
        if not day_transactions:
            raise SafeFailure(
                f"No Transaction Ledger entries found for target date {target_str}. "
                "Per the 'Missing Source of Truth' rule, refusing to fabricate a brief. "
                "Re-run with --target-date once the ledger has entries for the intended day."
            )

        cash_summary = build_cash_summary(day_transactions)
        variances = build_budget_variances(transactions, budget, target_date)
        unresolved = build_unresolved_queue(cash_summary)

        os.makedirs(f"{out_dir}/normalized", exist_ok=True)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/transactions.csv", TRANSACTIONS_FIELDS, transactions)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/budget.csv", BUDGET_FIELDS, budget)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/revenue.csv", REVENUE_FIELDS, revenue)

        generated_at = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"
        report = render_report(target_date, cash_summary, variances, unresolved, fetched, generated_at)
        with open(f"{out_dir}/report.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(report)

        print(f"Wrote {out_dir}/normalized/transactions.csv, budget.csv, revenue.csv, and report.md", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0

    except SafeFailure as exc:
        print(f"SAFE FAILURE: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

        with FixtureServer({"/t/d/TXN1": ("text/csv", b"a,b\\n1,2\\n")}) as server:

        self._routes = routes
        handler = _make_handler(routes)
        self._httpd = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    @property
    def port(self) -> int:
        return self._httpd.server_port

    def url(self, path: str) -> str:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{path}"

    def __enter__(self) -> "FixtureServer":
        self._thread.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc_info) -> None:
        self._httpd.shutdown()
        self._httpd.server_close()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)

                self.end_headers()

            content_type, body = route
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

            pass  # keep test output quiet

+"""Minimal local HTTP fixture server for exercising generate_brief.py's
+fetch path without hitting real Google Sheets.
+
+Standard-library only, matching the rest of this skill's scripts.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import http.server
+import threading
+import urllib.parse
+
+
+class _NoReverseDnsHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
+    """Skips the reverse-DNS lookup HTTPServer.server_bind() normally does
+    via socket.getfqdn() -- on a machine with no reachable DNS that lookup
+    can block for tens of seconds per server, even for 127.0.0.1."""
+
+    def server_bind(self) -> None:
+        import socketserver
+
+        socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind(self)
+        host, port = self.server_address[:2]
+        self.server_name = host
+        self.server_port = port
+
+
+class FixtureServer:
+    """Serves canned CSV (or other) bodies on 127.0.0.1.
+
+    Routes are keyed by the sheet's "/d/<id>" base path (what you'd pass as
+    --transactions-url etc.) -- export_csv_url() turns that into
+    "<base>/export?format=csv[&gid=...]", and this server strips the
+    "/export" suffix and query string before matching, so the route key
+    stays exactly the URL you handed to generate_brief.
+
+    Usage:
+        with FixtureServer({"/t/d/TXN1": ("text/csv", b"a,b\\n1,2\\n")}) as server:
+            url = server.url("/t/d/TXN1")
+            ...
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, routes: dict[str, tuple[str, bytes]]):
+        self._routes = routes
+        handler = _make_handler(routes)
+        self._httpd = _NoReverseDnsHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
+        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
+
+    @property
+    def port(self) -> int:
+        return self._httpd.server_port
+
+    def url(self, path: str) -> str:
+        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{path}"
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> "FixtureServer":
+        self._thread.start()
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, *exc_info) -> None:
+        self._httpd.shutdown()
+        self._httpd.server_close()
+        self._thread.join(timeout=5)
+
+
+def _make_handler(routes: dict[str, tuple[str, bytes]]):
+    class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib method name)
+            path = urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path).path
+            if path.endswith("/export"):
+                path = path[: -len("/export")]
+            route = routes.get(path)
+            if route is None:
+                self.send_response(404)
+                self.end_headers()
+                return
+            content_type, body = route
+            self.send_response(200)
+            self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
+            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
+            self.end_headers()
+            self.wfile.write(body)
+
+        def log_message(self, format: str, *args) -> None:  # noqa: A002
+            pass  # keep test output quiet
+
+    return Handler

business-rule notes, and a self-checking Definition-of-Done gate.

Fetch evidence (URL / spreadsheet ID / tab / timestamp / source_version /
row count for each of the three sheets) is also printed to stderr *before*
any deliverable file is written, so the run log captures proof of a live
read independent of the committed report.

## Validation and safe-failure behavior

The script never silently substitutes stale, cached, or partial data. It
exits non-zero and writes **no** deliverables (existing ones are left
untouched) when:

- A sheet fetch fails (network error, non-200 status), returns something
  that isn't a plain CSV (wrong content-type, or an HTML/sign-in page —
  usually a sharing-permission problem), or its header doesn't fingerprint
  to any known role.
- The Transaction Ledger has zero rows dated `--target-date` ("Missing
  Source of Truth" — most often because the sheet hasn't been updated yet,
  or the default previous-business-day has no data and no override was
  given).
- A target-date transaction's `status` isn't one of `posted` / `pending` /

---
name: daily-financial-health-brief
description: Freshly fetches Quillhaven Academy's Transaction Ledger, Budget Targets, and Revenue Snapshot Google Sheets, normalizes them into CSV, and drafts the daily/MTD financial health brief (cash summary, material budget variances, unresolved items) for the Finance and Operations Manager. Activate when asked to prepare, refresh, regenerate, or reproduce Quillhaven Academy's daily financial health brief, or to normalize/reconcile its three source sheets against the monthly budget.
---

# Daily Financial Health Brief

Turns Quillhaven Academy's three live Google Sheets into normalized CSVs and a
concise Markdown management brief, in one reproducible run.

## Runtime and dependencies

- Python 3.9+ (standard library only — no third-party packages required).
  - Tested with the macOS system interpreter (`/usr/bin/python3`) and Homebrew Python.
  - If you hit `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` (common on python.org "framework"
    builds whose trust store isn't wired to the OS), either run that Python's
    `Install Certificates.command`, or `pip install certifi` — the script
    auto-detects and uses certifi's CA bundle when it's importable.
- Network access to `docs.google.com` (outbound HTTPS only). No credentials,
  API keys, or OAuth are needed: the three sheets are shared "Anyone with the
  link – Viewer."

## Inputs: the three Sheets and how their roles are identified

The skill fetches these three viewer-only Google Sheets on **every run** —
never a bundled, downloaded, or previously cached CSV:

| Role | Default URL |
|---|---|
| Transaction Ledger | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Budget Targets | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Revenue Snapshot | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |

Each URL is converted to its CSV export endpoint
(`.../export?format=csv[&gid=…]`) and fetched fresh. The skill does **not**
trust the URL's declared role or argument position: it fingerprints each
fetched sheet's header row and assigns a role by the columns actually present
(`transaction_id`+`amount`+`status` → transactions; `budget_amount`+`period`
→ budget; `metric`+`value` → revenue). This keeps the run correct even if
column order, source names, or extra columns change, or if two URLs are
passed out of order.

The three URLs are overridable — pass different Sheet URLs (e.g. a test
fixture, or next month's sheets) via `--transactions-url`, `--budget-url`,
`--revenue-url` without editing the script.

## Execution command

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 daily-financial-health-brief/scripts/generate_brief.py \
  --target-date 2026-08-11
```

- `--target-date YYYY-MM-DD` (optional): the day to brief on. **Defaults to
  the previous business day relative to the run date** (weekends skipped;
  no holiday calendar is encoded — a holiday will need an explicit
  `--target-date` or a future enhancement here).
- `--transactions-url` / `--budget-url` / `--revenue-url` (optional):
  override any of the three default Sheet URLs.
- `--out-dir` (optional): defaults to `deliverables/` at the repository root.

Re-running with the same source snapshot and the same `--target-date`
produces byte-for-byte identical `report.md` content (all aggregation uses
`Decimal` arithmetic and sorted iteration order — no floating point, no
wall-clock-dependent values baked into the numbers).

## Outputs

- `deliverables/normalized/transactions.csv` — every Transaction Ledger row, columns:
  `transaction_id, date, account, category, description, amount, currency, status, source, source_version, amount_status`.
- `deliverables/normalized/budget.csv` — every Budget Targets row, columns:
  `period, category, budget_amount, currency, owner, review_rule, source, source_version`.
- `deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv` — every Revenue Snapshot row, columns:
  `date, source, metric, value, currency, source_version`.
- `deliverables/report.md` — the daily brief: Cash Summary, Material Budget
  Variances, Unresolved Items Queue, source fetch evidence (URL, spreadsheet
  ID, tab, fetch timestamp, source_version, row count per sheet),
  business-rule notes, and a self-checking Definition-of-Done gate.

Fetch evidence (URL / spreadsheet ID / tab / timestamp / source_version /
row count for each of the three sheets) is also printed to stderr *before*
any deliverable file is written, so the run log captures proof of a live
read independent of the committed report.

## Validation and safe-failure behavior

The script never silently substitutes stale, cached, or partial data. It
exits non-zero and writes **no** deliverables (existing ones are left
untouched) when:

- A sheet fetch fails (network error, non-200 status), returns something
  that isn't a plain CSV (wrong content-type, or an HTML/sign-in page —
  usually a sharing-permission problem), or its header doesn't fingerprint
  to any known role.
- The Transaction Ledger has zero rows dated `--target-date` ("Missing
  Source of Truth" — most often because the sheet hasn't been updated yet,
  or the default previous-business-day has no data and no override was
  given).
- A target-date transaction's `status` isn't one of `posted` / `pending` /
  `disputed` (needs manual categorization before the run can continue).

Business rules for what counts as a "material" variance, how unknown
amounts and negative values are handled, and which decisions came directly
from the Finance and Operations Manager are in
[`references/business-rules.md`](references/business-rules.md).

# Business Rules (from the Finance and Operations Manager interview)

These rules are encoded in `../scripts/generate_brief.py`. This file exists
so an operator can audit *why* the script behaves as it does without reading
the code, and so future changes stay consistent with what was actually
requested.

## Cash categorization

- Posted, Pending, and Disputed cash are always three **separate** totals.
  Never net them into one cash figure — the manager's workflow depends on
  seeing each status independently.
- Negative amounts are preserved exactly as signed values and labeled
  "Credit/Correction" — never flipped to positive, never dropped.
- A transaction whose `status` is anything other than `posted`, `pending`,
  or `disputed` blocks the run (needs a human to assign the correct
  category before the brief can be trusted).

## Unknown or blank amounts

- A transaction with a blank/unparseable `amount` keeps its status for
  visibility but is **excluded from every numeric total** — cash totals and
  MTD budget totals alike. Never assumed to be zero, never estimated.
- It is still surfaced by transaction ID in the report's Unresolved Items
  Queue, marked "Amount Unknown," for escalation.

## Materiality threshold

- A budget variance is "material" only if it is **strictly greater than
  both** 10% of the department's monthly budget **and** USD 500 in absolute
  dollar terms. Both conditions are strict inequalities — a variance sitting
  at exactly 10% or exactly $500 does **not** qualify. (The August 2026 data
  contains real examples that land exactly on each boundary; the script's
  test run confirms both are correctly excluded.)
- Report language uses exact dollar amounts, department names, and
  percentages — never qualitative words like "large" or "unusual."

## Month-to-date budget comparison

- MTD spend per department is summed from **Transaction Ledger rows with
  `status = posted`** only, for the target date's calendar month through
  the target date, grouped by `category`. This is compared against
  `Budget Targets.budget_amount` for the matching `period`.
- The Revenue Snapshot sheet is **not** an input to this comparison. Per
  the manager: Revenue Snapshot is used for dated revenue and
  outstanding-balance comparisons, a separate concern from expense-vs-budget
  reconciliation. It is still normalized to `deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv`
  for that separate use and for traceability.

## Starting/closing cash balance reconciliation — intentionally out of scope

An earlier draft of the reporting spec called for comparing the prior day's
starting cash balance against the previous day's closing balance, and
pausing on any mismatch. The manager clarified this is **not** how the
actual daily brief works: because Posted/Pending/Disputed are never netted
into one cash total (see above), there is no single "cash balance" to
reconcile day-over-day in the first place. This script does not implement
that check, and none of the three source sheets carries a balance field —
so there is nothing to compare even if it were requested later.

## Escalation without an interactive operator

The original spec described "pause and ask the Finance and Operations
Manager" for out-of-band items (unknown amounts, uncategorized statuses).
This script runs non-interactively (e.g. on a schedule), so it implements
that intent as **fail-safe, not fail-silent**:

- Recoverable-by-listing items (unknown amounts) are still written into the
  report's Unresolved Items Queue for a human to review and resolve —
  the run completes.
- Non-recoverable items (a transaction status the script doesn't recognize,
  a sheet that won't fetch as valid CSV, no ledger rows for the target date)
  stop the run entirely with a clear message on stderr and **no** deliverable
  files are written or overwritten. A human reruns once the underlying data
  or configuration is fixed.

def build_budget_variances(all_transactions: list[dict], budget_rows: list[dict], target_date: dt.date) -> list[dict]:
    month_prefix = target_date.strftime("%Y-%m")
    target_str = target_date.isoformat()

    mtd_posted = defaultdict(lambda: Decimal("0"))
    mtd_txn_ids = defaultdict(list)
    for txn in all_transactions:
        date_str = txn["date"]
        if not date_str.startswith(month_prefix) or date_str > target_str:
            continue
        if (txn["status"] or "").strip().lower() != "posted":
            continue
        amount = parse_amount(txn["amount"])
        if amount is None:
            continue  # never assume zero for an unknown amount
        category = txn["category"]
        mtd_posted[category] += amount
        mtd_txn_ids[category].append(txn["transaction_id"])

    budget_by_category = {}
    for row in budget_rows:
        if row["period"] == month_prefix:
            budget_amount = parse_amount(row["budget_amount"])
            if budget_amount is not None:
                budget_by_category[row["category"]] = budget_amount

    variances = []
    for category in sorted(budget_by_category):
        budget_amount = budget_by_category[category]
        spend = mtd_posted.get(category, Decimal("0"))
        variance = spend - budget_amount
        pct = (abs(variance) / budget_amount * 100) if budget_amount != 0 else None
        material = (
            budget_amount != 0
            and pct is not None
            and pct > (MATERIALITY_PCT * 100)
            and abs(variance) > MATERIALITY_USD
        )
        variances.append({
            "category": category,
            "budget": budget_amount,
            "mtd_posted": spend,
            "variance": variance,
            "pct": pct,
            "material": material,
            "txn_ids": sorted(mtd_txn_ids.get(category, [])),
        })
    return variances

def build_budget_variances(all_transactions: list[dict], budget_rows: list[dict], target_date: dt.date) -> list[dict]:
    month_prefix = target_date.strftime("%Y-%m")
    target_str = target_date.isoformat()

    mtd_posted = defaultdict(lambda: Decimal("0"))
    mtd_txn_ids = defaultdict(list)
    for txn in all_transactions:
        date_str = txn["date"]
        if not date_str.startswith(month_prefix) or date_str > target_str:
            continue
        if (txn["status"] or "").strip().lower() != "posted":
            continue
        amount = parse_amount(txn["amount"])
        if amount is None:
            continue  # never assume zero for an unknown amount
        category = txn["category"]
        mtd_posted[category] += amount
        mtd_txn_ids[category].append(txn["transaction_id"])

    budget_by_category = {}
    for row in budget_rows:
        if row["period"] == month_prefix:
            budget_amount = parse_amount(row["budget_amount"])
            if budget_amount is not None:
                budget_by_category[row["category"]] = budget_amount

    variances = []
    for category in sorted(budget_by_category):
        budget_amount = budget_by_category[category]
        spend = mtd_posted.get(category, Decimal("0"))
        variance = spend - budget_amount
        pct = (abs(variance) / budget_amount * 100) if budget_amount != 0 else None
        material = (
            budget_amount != 0
            and pct is not None
            and pct > (MATERIALITY_PCT * 100)
            and abs(variance) > MATERIALITY_USD
        )
        variances.append({
            "category": category,
            "budget": budget_amount,
            "mtd_posted": spend,
            "variance": variance,
            "pct": pct,
            "material": material,
            "txn_ids": sorted(mtd_txn_ids.get(category, [])),
        })
    return variances

    sign = "-" if value < 0 else ""

"""Covers two gaps identified in generate_brief.py's business logic:

1. amount_status mismatch: the Transaction Ledger carries an amount_status
   column alongside amount, but the script used to determine known/unknown
   purely by trying to parse amount, ignoring amount_status entirely. If the
   two signals ever disagreed, the parse-based result silently won. Now any
   disagreement is treated as unknown (never trusting either side alone) and
   is excluded from both cash totals and MTD budget spend.

2. Orphan category: a department with real posted spend but no matching
   Budget Targets row for the period used to vanish from the report with no
   trace. build_budget_variances() now also returns the orphaned categories
   so they can be surfaced in their own report section instead of silently
   dropped.

These are pure business-logic checks against build_cash_summary() and
build_budget_variances() directly -- no network or fixture server involved.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import os
import sys
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "scripts"))

from generate_brief import build_budget_variances, build_cash_summary  # noqa: E402


def make_txn(**overrides) -> dict:
    txn = {
        "transaction_id": "TX-DEFAULT",
        "date": "2026-01-02",
        "account": "Checking",
        "category": "Insurance",
        "description": "Test row",
        "amount": "500.00",
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "posted",
        "source": "test",
        "source_version": "v1",
        "amount_status": "confirmed",
    }
    txn.update(overrides)
    return txn


class AmountStatusMismatchTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parseable_amount_declared_unknown_is_excluded_from_cash_totals(self):
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-A", amount="500.00", amount_status="unknown")
        summary = build_cash_summary([txn])

        self.assertEqual(summary["buckets"]["posted"], [])
        self.assertEqual(summary["totals"]["posted"], Decimal("0"))
        self.assertEqual(len(summary["unknown_amount"]), 1)
        flagged_txn, reason = summary["unknown_amount"][0]
        self.assertEqual(flagged_txn["transaction_id"], "TX-A")
        self.assertEqual(reason, "amount_status mismatch")

    def test_unparseable_amount_declared_confirmed_is_also_a_mismatch(self):
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-B", amount="not-a-number", amount_status="confirmed")
        summary = build_cash_summary([txn])

        self.assertEqual(summary["totals"]["posted"], Decimal("0"))
        flagged_txn, reason = summary["unknown_amount"][0]
        self.assertEqual(flagged_txn["transaction_id"], "TX-B")
        self.assertEqual(reason, "amount_status mismatch")

    def test_blank_amount_declared_unknown_agrees_and_is_plain_blank(self):
        # Sanity check: when the two signals agree that the amount is
        # unknown, it must be labeled "amount blank", not a mismatch --
        # proving the mismatch label above is actually conditioned on a
        # real disagreement, not applied unconditionally.
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-C", amount="", amount_status="unknown")
        summary = build_cash_summary([txn])

        flagged_txn, reason = summary["unknown_amount"][0]
        self.assertEqual(flagged_txn["transaction_id"], "TX-C")
        self.assertEqual(reason, "amount blank")

    def test_mismatch_is_also_excluded_from_mtd_budget_spend(self):
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-D", amount="500.00", amount_status="unknown",
                        category="Insurance", status="posted")
        budget_rows = [{"period": "2026-01", "category": "Insurance", "budget_amount": "1000"}]

        result = build_budget_variances([txn], budget_rows, dt.date(2026, 1, 2))

        self.assertEqual(len(result["variances"]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["variances"][0]["mtd_posted"], Decimal("0"))
        self.assertEqual(result["orphan_categories"], [])


class OrphanCategoryTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_posted_spend_with_no_budget_line_is_an_orphan_not_a_variance(self):
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-E", category="Catering", amount="750.00",
                        amount_status="confirmed", status="posted")

        result = build_budget_variances([txn], [], dt.date(2026, 1, 2))

        self.assertEqual(result["variances"], [])
        self.assertEqual(len(result["orphan_categories"]), 1)
        orphan = result["orphan_categories"][0]
        self.assertEqual(orphan["category"], "Catering")
        self.assertEqual(orphan["mtd_posted"], Decimal("750.00"))
        self.assertEqual(orphan["txn_ids"], ["TX-E"])

    def test_category_with_a_budget_line_is_not_also_reported_as_an_orphan(self):
        txn = make_txn(transaction_id="TX-F", category="Insurance", amount="500.00",
                        amount_status="confirmed", status="posted")
        budget_rows = [{"period": "2026-01", "category": "Insurance", "budget_amount": "1000"}]

        result = build_budget_variances([txn], budget_rows, dt.date(2026, 1, 2))

        self.assertEqual(result["orphan_categories"], [])
        self.assertEqual(len(result["variances"]), 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

message.content: the Leaderboard tab's challenge description requires "daily posted totals and their signed change" compared against a "comparison date" — e.g., reporting date Aug 11 vs. comparison Aug 10. Nothing in the current code implements this at all. I went back to the Work Sim interview and asked why the exact dates matter, and learned that the manager "strictly" uses the dates specified in each request for financial consistency and alignment with the review period. --comparison-date should be a required explicit argument with no silent default — fail safely if it's missing, same pattern as a missing source. And if the comparison date has zero transactions, that's safe to flag ("no comparison data available") rather than fail the whole run, since it doesn't corrupt anything else in the report.

---
name: daily-financial-health-brief
description: Freshly fetches Quillhaven Academy's Transaction Ledger, Budget Targets, and Revenue Snapshot Google Sheets, normalizes them into CSV, and drafts the daily/MTD financial health brief (cash summary, material budget variances, unresolved items) for the Finance and Operations Manager. Activate when asked to prepare, refresh, regenerate, or reproduce Quillhaven Academy's daily financial health brief, or to normalize/reconcile its three source sheets against the monthly budget.
---

# Daily Financial Health Brief

Turns Quillhaven Academy's three live Google Sheets into normalized CSVs and a
concise Markdown management brief, in one reproducible run.

## Runtime and dependencies

- Python 3.9+ (standard library only — no third-party packages required).
  - Tested with the macOS system interpreter (`/usr/bin/python3`) and Homebrew Python.
  - If you hit `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` (common on python.org "framework"
    builds whose trust store isn't wired to the OS), either run that Python's
    `Install Certificates.command`, or `pip install certifi` — the script
    auto-detects and uses certifi's CA bundle when it's importable.
- Network access to `docs.google.com` (outbound HTTPS only). No credentials,
  API keys, or OAuth are needed: the three sheets are shared "Anyone with the
  link – Viewer."

## Inputs: the three Sheets and how their roles are identified

The skill fetches these three viewer-only Google Sheets on **every run** —
never a bundled, downloaded, or previously cached CSV:

| Role | Default URL |
|---|---|
| Transaction Ledger | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Budget Targets | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Revenue Snapshot | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |

Each URL is converted to its CSV export endpoint
(`.../export?format=csv[&gid=…]`) and fetched fresh. The skill does **not**
trust the URL's declared role or argument position: it fingerprints each
fetched sheet's header row and assigns a role by the columns actually present
(`transaction_id`+`amount`+`status` → transactions; `budget_amount`+`period`
→ budget; `metric`+`value` → revenue). This keeps the run correct even if
column order, source names, or extra columns change, or if two URLs are
passed out of order.

The three URLs are overridable — pass different Sheet URLs (e.g. a test
fixture, or next month's sheets) via `--transactions-url`, `--budget-url`,
`--revenue-url` without editing the script.

## Execution command

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 daily-financial-health-brief/scripts/generate_brief.py \
  --target-date 2026-08-11
```

- `--target-date YYYY-MM-DD` (optional): the day to brief on. **Defaults to
  the previous business day relative to the run date** (weekends skipped;
  no holiday calendar is encoded — a holiday will need an explicit
  `--target-date` or a future enhancement here).
- `--transactions-url` / `--budget-url` / `--revenue-url` (optional):
  override any of the three default Sheet URLs.
- `--out-dir` (optional): defaults to `deliverables/` at the repository root.

Re-running with the same source snapshot and the same `--target-date`
produces byte-for-byte identical `report.md` content (all aggregation uses
`Decimal` arithmetic and sorted iteration order — no floating point, no
wall-clock-dependent values baked into the numbers).

## Outputs

- `deliverables/normalized/transactions.csv` — every Transaction Ledger row, columns:
  `transaction_id, date, account, category, description, amount, currency, status, source, source_version, amount_status`.
- `deliverables/normalized/budget.csv` — every Budget Targets row, columns:
  `period, category, budget_amount, currency, owner, review_rule, source, source_version`.
- `deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv` — every Revenue Snapshot row, columns:
  `date, source, metric, value, currency, source_version`.
- `deliverables/report.md` — the daily brief: Cash Summary, Material Budget
  Variances, Unresolved Items Queue, source fetch evidence (URL, spreadsheet
  ID, tab, fetch timestamp, source_version, row count per sheet),
  business-rule notes, and a self-checking Definition-of-Done gate.

Fetch evidence (URL / spreadsheet ID / tab / timestamp / source_version /
row count for each of the three sheets) is also printed to stderr *before*
any deliverable file is written, so the run log captures proof of a live
read independent of the committed report.

## Validation and safe-failure behavior

The script never silently substitutes stale, cached, or partial data. It
exits non-zero and writes **no** deliverables (existing ones are left
untouched) when:

- A sheet fetch fails (network error, non-200 status), returns something
  that isn't a plain CSV (wrong content-type, or an HTML/sign-in page —
  usually a sharing-permission problem), or its header doesn't fingerprint
  to any known role.
- The Transaction Ledger has zero rows dated `--target-date` ("Missing
  Source of Truth" — most often because the sheet hasn't been updated yet,
  or the default previous-business-day has no data and no override was
  given).
- A target-date transaction's `status` isn't one of `posted` / `pending` /
  `disputed` (needs manual categorization before the run can continue).

### Testing safe-failure paths

Two of the safe-failure checks above are hard to exercise against the real
sheets, so `tests/` covers them against a local HTTP fixture server instead
(`tests/fixture_server.py`) — no real sheet access or network needed:

- **Bad-status row with a valid amount** — a transaction with a non-blank,
  parseable `amount` but a `status` outside `posted`/`pending`/`disputed`
  must raise `SafeFailure`. The amount has to be non-blank: a blank/
  unparseable amount routes the row to `unknown_amount` *before* the status
  is ever checked, so a blank-amount version of the same bad status is
  included as a sanity check that must **not** raise.
- **Role-mismatch header** — a sheet whose header doesn't fingerprint to
  any of transactions/budget/revenue must raise `SafeFailure`. No special
  row is needed; the header alone decides this.

Run from `daily-financial-health-brief/`:

```
python3 -m unittest tests.test_untestable_paths -v
```

Business rules for what counts as a "material" variance, how unknown
amounts and negative values are handled, and which decisions came directly
from the Finance and Operations Manager are in
[`references/business-rules.md`](references/business-rules.md).

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--transactions-url", default=DEFAULT_URLS["transactions"])
    parser.add_argument("--budget-url", default=DEFAULT_URLS["budget"])
    parser.add_argument("--revenue-url", default=DEFAULT_URLS["revenue"])
    parser.add_argument(
        "--target-date",
        default=None,
        help="YYYY-MM-DD to brief on. Defaults to the previous business day "
             "relative to the run date (weekends skipped; no holiday calendar).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--out-dir",
        default=None,
        help="Deliverables directory. Defaults to <skill-root>/../deliverables.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)

    skill_root = __file__.rsplit("/scripts/", 1)[0]
    out_dir = args.out_dir or f"{skill_root}/../deliverables"

    urls = {
        "transactions": args.transactions_url,
        "budget": args.budget_url,
        "revenue": args.revenue_url,
    }

    try:
        fetched = fetch_all(urls)

        for role in ("transactions", "budget", "revenue"):
            meta = fetched[role]
            versions = sorted({row.get("source_version", "") for row in meta["rows"] if row.get("source_version")})
            meta["source_versions"] = ", ".join(versions) if versions else "n/a"
            print(
                f"[fetch-evidence] role={role} url={meta['sheet_url']} "
                f"spreadsheet_id={meta['spreadsheet_id']} tab={meta['tab_identity']} "
                f"fetched_at={meta['fetched_at']} row_count={meta['row_count']} "
                f"source_version={meta['source_versions']}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )

        transactions = normalize_rows(fetched["transactions"]["rows"], TRANSACTIONS_FIELDS)
        budget = normalize_rows(fetched["budget"]["rows"], BUDGET_FIELDS)
        revenue = normalize_rows(fetched["revenue"]["rows"], REVENUE_FIELDS)

        if args.target_date:
            target_date = dt.date.fromisoformat(args.target_date)
        else:
            target_date = previous_business_day(dt.date.today())
        target_str = target_date.isoformat()

        day_transactions = [t for t in transactions if t["date"] == target_str]
        if not day_transactions:
            raise SafeFailure(
                f"No Transaction Ledger entries found for target date {target_str}. "
                "Per the 'Missing Source of Truth' rule, refusing to fabricate a brief. "
                "Re-run with --target-date once the ledger has entries for the intended day."
            )

        cash_summary = build_cash_summary(day_transactions)
        budget_result = build_budget_variances(transactions, budget, target_date)
        variances = budget_result["variances"]
        orphan_categories = budget_result["orphan_categories"]
        unresolved = build_unresolved_queue(cash_summary)

        os.makedirs(f"{out_dir}/normalized", exist_ok=True)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/transactions.csv", TRANSACTIONS_FIELDS, transactions)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/budget.csv", BUDGET_FIELDS, budget)
        write_csv(f"{out_dir}/normalized/revenue.csv", REVENUE_FIELDS, revenue)

        generated_at = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"
        report = render_report(
            target_date, cash_summary, variances, orphan_categories, unresolved, fetched, generated_at
        )
        with open(f"{out_dir}/report.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(report)

        print(f"Wrote {out_dir}/normalized/transactions.csv, budget.csv, revenue.csv, and report.md", file=sys.stderr)

    comparison_str = comparison_date.isoformat()

        comparison_total = comparison_summary["totals"]["posted"]
        signed_change = target_posted_total - comparison_total

"""Exercises two generate_brief.py failure paths that previously could not
be tested without hitting real Google Sheets:

1. A transaction row with a non-blank, parseable amount but an
   unrecognized status -> build_cash_summary() must raise SafeFailure.
   Subtlety: if the amount were blank/unparseable instead, the row would
   be routed to "unknown_amount" and the status check is never reached
   (see generate_brief.build_cash_summary) -- so the fixture row MUST
   carry a real amount, or this path silently stops being exercised.

2. A sheet whose header doesn't fingerprint as transactions/budget/
   revenue -> detect_role() must raise SafeFailure. No special row is
   needed here: the header alone determines the role, so any wrong set
   of columns reproduces it.

Uses a local HTTP fixture server (tests/fixture_server.py) so no network
access or real spreadsheet is involved, relying on export_csv_url()
preserving the request's own host/path instead of rewriting everything
to docs.google.com.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))

import generate_brief  # noqa: E402
from fixture_server import FixtureServer  # noqa: E402

VALID_BUDGET_CSV = (
    "period,category,budget_amount,currency,owner,review_rule,source,source_version\n"
    "2026-01,Insurance,1000,USD,Jane,manual,test-fixture,v1\n"
).encode("utf-8")

VALID_REVENUE_CSV = (
    "date,source,metric,value,currency,source_version\n"
    "2026-01-02,Online,Tuition,500,USD,v1\n"
).encode("utf-8")


def run_main(urls: dict[str, str], target_date: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as out_dir:
        argv = [
            "--transactions-url", urls["transactions"],
            "--budget-url", urls["budget"],
            "--revenue-url", urls["revenue"],
            "--target-date", target_date,
            "--out-dir", out_dir,
        ]
        stderr = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
            rc = generate_brief.main(argv)
        return rc, stderr.getvalue()


class BadStatusRowTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_blank_amount_with_unrecognized_status_is_a_safe_failure(self):
        transactions_csv = (
            "transaction_id,date,account,category,description,amount,currency,"
            "status,source,source_version,amount_status\n"
            "TXN100,2026-01-02,Checking,Insurance,Test bad status,100.00,USD,"
            "voided,test-fixture,v1,ok\n"
        ).encode("utf-8")

        routes = {
            "/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN": ("text/csv", transactions_csv),
            "/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD": ("text/csv", VALID_BUDGET_CSV),
            "/r/d/FIXTURE_REV": ("text/csv", VALID_REVENUE_CSV),
        }
        with FixtureServer(routes) as server:
            urls = {
                "transactions": server.url("/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN"),
                "budget": server.url("/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD"),
                "revenue": server.url("/r/d/FIXTURE_REV"),
            }
            rc, stderr = run_main(urls, "2026-01-02")

        self.assertEqual(rc, 1, stderr)
        self.assertIn("SAFE FAILURE", stderr)
        self.assertIn("TXN100", stderr)
        self.assertIn("unrecognized status", stderr)
        self.assertIn("voided", stderr)

    def test_blank_amount_with_unrecognized_status_does_not_trigger_the_check(self):
        # Sanity check for the subtlety noted in the module docstring: a
        # blank amount routes to unknown_amount *before* the status is
        # ever inspected, so this must NOT raise -- it proves the first
        # test's failure really comes from the status check, not from an
        # unrelated row-parsing error.
        transactions_csv = (
            "transaction_id,date,account,category,description,amount,currency,"
            "status,source,source_version,amount_status\n"
            "TXN101,2026-01-02,Checking,Insurance,Test blank amount,,USD,"
            "voided,test-fixture,v1,blank\n"
        ).encode("utf-8")

        routes = {
            "/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN": ("text/csv", transactions_csv),
            "/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD": ("text/csv", VALID_BUDGET_CSV),
            "/r/d/FIXTURE_REV": ("text/csv", VALID_REVENUE_CSV),
        }
        with FixtureServer(routes) as server:
            urls = {
                "transactions": server.url("/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN"),
                "budget": server.url("/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD"),
                "revenue": server.url("/r/d/FIXTURE_REV"),
            }
            rc, stderr = run_main(urls, "2026-01-02")

        self.assertEqual(rc, 0, stderr)


class RoleMismatchTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_header_that_matches_no_known_role_is_a_safe_failure(self):
        # Wrong columns entirely -- no transaction_id/amount/status,
        # budget_amount/period, or metric/value fingerprint. No special
        # row needed; the header alone decides this.
        mismatched_csv = b"name,quantity,price\nWidget,3,9.99\n"

        routes = {
            "/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN": ("text/csv", mismatched_csv),
            "/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD": ("text/csv", VALID_BUDGET_CSV),
            "/r/d/FIXTURE_REV": ("text/csv", VALID_REVENUE_CSV),
        }
        with FixtureServer(routes) as server:
            urls = {
                "transactions": server.url("/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN"),
                "budget": server.url("/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD"),
                "revenue": server.url("/r/d/FIXTURE_REV"),
            }
            rc, stderr = run_main(urls, "2026-01-02")

        self.assertEqual(rc, 1, stderr)
        self.assertIn("SAFE FAILURE", stderr)
        self.assertIn("Could not identify the role", stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Covers the Leaderboard challenge's "daily posted totals and their signed
change" requirement: comparing --target-date's Posted cash total against a
--comparison-date.

Per the Work Sim interview, the Finance and Operations Manager strictly uses
the exact dates given in each request -- never an inferred or defaulted
one -- for financial consistency and alignment with the review period. So:

- --comparison-date is a required, explicit CLI argument with no silent
  default. Missing it is a SafeFailure, exercised here end-to-end via the
  local fixture server (same pattern as tests/test_untestable_paths.py).
- A comparison date with zero Transaction Ledger rows does NOT fail the
  run -- it doesn't corrupt anything else in the report, so it's flagged
  ("no comparison data available") instead. Covered as a direct unit test
  against build_posted_comparison().
- The signed change itself (target total - comparison total) is covered
  as a direct unit test too.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import datetime as dt
import io
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))

import generate_brief  # noqa: E402
from fixture_server import FixtureServer  # noqa: E402

TRANSACTIONS_CSV = (
    "transaction_id,date,account,category,description,amount,currency,"
    "status,source,source_version,amount_status\n"
    "TX-1,2026-01-02,Checking,Insurance,Target day,1000.00,USD,"
    "posted,test-fixture,v1,confirmed\n"
).encode("utf-8")

BUDGET_CSV = (
    "period,category,budget_amount,currency,owner,review_rule,source,source_version\n"
    "2026-01,Insurance,1000,USD,Jane,manual,test-fixture,v1\n"
).encode("utf-8")

REVENUE_CSV = (
    "date,source,metric,value,currency,source_version\n"
    "2026-01-02,Online,Tuition,500,USD,v1\n"
).encode("utf-8")


def run_main(extra_args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
    routes = {
        "/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN": ("text/csv", TRANSACTIONS_CSV),
        "/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD": ("text/csv", BUDGET_CSV),
        "/r/d/FIXTURE_REV": ("text/csv", REVENUE_CSV),
    }
    with FixtureServer(routes) as server, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as out_dir:
        argv = [
            "--transactions-url", server.url("/t/d/FIXTURE_TXN"),
            "--budget-url", server.url("/b/d/FIXTURE_BUD"),
            "--revenue-url", server.url("/r/d/FIXTURE_REV"),
            "--target-date", "2026-01-02",
            "--out-dir", out_dir,
            *extra_args,
        ]
        stderr = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
            rc = generate_brief.main(argv)
        report_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "report.md")
        report = ""
        if os.path.exists(report_path):
            with open(report_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                report = handle.read()
        return rc, stderr.getvalue(), report


class RequiredArgumentTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_comparison_date_is_a_safe_failure(self):
        rc, stderr, report = run_main([])

        self.assertEqual(rc, 1, stderr)
        self.assertIn("SAFE FAILURE", stderr)
        self.assertIn("--comparison-date is required", stderr)
        self.assertEqual(report, "")

# Business Rules (from the Finance and Operations Manager interview)

These rules are encoded in `../scripts/generate_brief.py`. This file exists
so an operator can audit *why* the script behaves as it does without reading
the code, and so future changes stay consistent with what was actually
requested.

## Cash categorization

- Posted, Pending, and Disputed cash are always three **separate** totals.
  Never net them into one cash figure — the manager's workflow depends on
  seeing each status independently.
- Negative amounts are preserved exactly as signed values and labeled
  "Credit/Correction" — never flipped to positive, never dropped.
- A transaction whose `status` is anything other than `posted`, `pending`,
  or `disputed` blocks the run (needs a human to assign the correct
  category before the brief can be trusted).

## Unknown or blank amounts

# Business Rules (from the Finance and Operations Manager interview)

These rules are encoded in `../scripts/generate_brief.py`. This file exists
so an operator can audit *why* the script behaves as it does without reading
the code, and so future changes stay consistent with what was actually
requested.

## Cash categorization

- Posted, Pending, and Disputed cash are always three **separate** totals.
  Never net them into one cash figure — the manager's workflow depends on
  seeing each status independently.
- Negative amounts are preserved exactly as signed values and labeled
  "Credit/Correction" — never flipped to positive, never dropped.
- A transaction whose `status` is anything other than `posted`, `pending`,
  or `disputed` blocks the run (needs a human to assign the correct
  category before the brief can be trusted).

## Unknown or blank amounts

- A transaction with a blank/unparseable `amount` keeps its status for
  visibility but is **excluded from every numeric total** — cash totals and
  MTD budget totals alike. Never assumed to be zero, never estimated.
- It is still surfaced by transaction ID in the report's Unresolved Items
  Queue, marked "Amount Unknown," for escalation.

## Materiality threshold

- A budget variance is "material" only if it is **strictly greater than
  both** 10% of the department's monthly budget **and** USD 500 in absolute
  dollar terms. Both conditions are strict inequalities — a variance sitting
  at exactly 10% or exactly $500 does **not** qualify. (The August 2026 data
  contains real examples that land exactly on each boundary; the script's
  test run confirms both are correctly excluded.)
- Report language uses exact dollar amounts, department names, and
  percentages — never qualitative words like "large" or "unusual."

## Month-to-date budget comparison

- MTD spend per department is summed from **Transaction Ledger rows with
  `status = posted`** only, for the target date's calendar month through
  the target date, grouped by `category`. This is compared against
  `Budget Targets.budget_amount` for the matching `period`.
- The Revenue Snapshot sheet is **not** an input to this comparison. Per
  the manager: Revenue Snapshot is used for dated revenue and
  outstanding-balance comparisons, a separate concern from expense-vs-budget
  reconciliation. It is still normalized to `deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv`
  for that separate use and for traceability.

## Starting/closing cash balance reconciliation — intentionally out of scope

An earlier draft of the reporting spec called for comparing the prior day's
starting cash balance against the previous day's closing balance, and
pausing on any mismatch. The manager clarified this is **not** how the
actual daily brief works: because Posted/Pending/Disputed are never netted
into one cash total (see above), there is no single "cash balance" to
reconcile day-over-day in the first place. This script does not implement
that check, and none of the three source sheets carries a balance field —
so there is nothing to compare even if it were requested later.

## Escalation without an interactive operator

The original spec described "pause and ask the Finance and Operations
Manager" for out-of-band items (unknown amounts, uncategorized statuses).
This script runs non-interactively (e.g. on a schedule), so it implements
that intent as **fail-safe, not fail-silent**:

- Recoverable-by-listing items (unknown amounts) are still written into the
  report's Unresolved Items Queue for a human to review and resolve —
  the run completes.
- Non-recoverable items (a transaction status the script doesn't recognize,
  a sheet that won't fetch as valid CSV, no ledger rows for the target date)
  stop the run entirely with a clear message on stderr and **no** deliverable
  files are written or overwritten. A human reruns once the underlying data
  or configuration is fixed.

# Daily Financial Health Brief

Turns Quillhaven Academy's three live Google Sheets into normalized CSVs and a
concise Markdown management brief, in one reproducible run.

## Runtime and dependencies

- Python 3.9+ (standard library only — no third-party packages required).
  - Tested with the macOS system interpreter (`/usr/bin/python3`) and Homebrew Python.
  - If you hit `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` (common on python.org "framework"
    builds whose trust store isn't wired to the OS), either run that Python's
    `Install Certificates.command`, or `pip install certifi` — the script
    auto-detects and uses certifi's CA bundle when it's importable.
- Network access to `docs.google.com` (outbound HTTPS only). No credentials,
  API keys, or OAuth are needed: the three sheets are shared "Anyone with the
  link – Viewer."

## Inputs: the three Sheets and how their roles are identified

The skill fetches these three viewer-only Google Sheets on **every run** —
never a bundled, downloaded, or previously cached CSV:

| Role | Default URL |
|---|---|
| Transaction Ledger | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Budget Targets | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |
| Revenue Snapshot | `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED` |

Each URL is converted to its CSV export endpoint
(`.../export?format=csv[&gid=…]`) and fetched fresh. The skill does **not**
trust the URL's declared role or argument position: it fingerprints each
fetched sheet's header row and assigns a role by the columns actually present
(`transaction_id`+`amount`+`status` → transactions; `budget_amount`+`period`
→ budget; `metric`+`value` → revenue). This keeps the run correct even if
column order, source names, or extra columns change, or if two URLs are
passed out of order.

The three URLs are overridable — pass different Sheet URLs (e.g. a test
fixture, or next month's sheets) via `--transactions-url`, `--budget-url`,
`--revenue-url` without editing the script.

## Execution command

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 daily-financial-health-brief/scripts/generate_brief.py \
  --target-date 2026-08-11
```

- `--target-date YYYY-MM-DD` (optional): the day to brief on. **Defaults to
  the previous business day relative to the run date** (weekends skipped;
  no holiday calendar is encoded — a holiday will need an explicit
  `--target-date` or a future enhancement here).
- `--transactions-url` / `--budget-url` / `--revenue-url` (optional):
  override any of the three default Sheet URLs.
- `--out-dir` (optional): defaults to `deliverables/` at the repository root.

Re-running with the same source snapshot and the same `--target-date`
produces byte-for-byte identical `report.md` content (all aggregation uses
`Decimal` arithmetic and sorted iteration order — no floating point, no
wall-clock-dependent values baked into the numbers).

## Outputs

- `deliverables/normalized/transactions.csv` — every Transaction Ledger row, columns:
  `transaction_id, date, account, category, description, amount, currency, status, source, source_version, amount_status`.
- `deliverables/normalized/budget.csv` — every Budget Targets row, columns:
  `period, category, budget_amount, currency, owner, review_rule, source, source_version`.
- `deliverables/normalized/revenue.csv` — every Revenue Snapshot row, columns:
  `date, source, metric, value, currency, source_version`.
- `deliverables/report.md` — the daily brief: Cash Summary, Material Budget
  Variances, Unresolved Items Queue, source fetch evidence (URL, spreadsheet
  ID, tab, fetch timestamp, source_version, row count per sheet),
  business-rule notes, and a self-checking Definition-of-Done gate.

Fetch evidence (URL / spreadsheet ID / tab / timestamp / source_version /
row count for each of the three sheets) is also printed to stderr *before*
any deliverable file is written, so the run log captures proof of a live
read independent of the committed report.

## Validation and safe-failure behavior

The script never silently substitutes stale, cached, or partial data. It
exits non-zero and writes **no** deliverables (existing ones are left
untouched) when:

- A sheet fetch fails (network error, non-200 status), returns something
  that isn't a plain CSV (wrong content-type, or an HTML/sign-in page —
  usually a sharing-permission problem), or its header doesn't fingerprint
  to any known role.
- The Transaction Ledger has zero rows dated `--target-date` ("Missing
  Source of Truth" — most often because the sheet hasn't been updated yet,
  or the default previous-business-day has no data and no override was
  given).
- A target-date transaction's `status` isn't one of `posted` / `pending` /
  `disputed` (needs manual categorization before the run can continue).

### Testing safe-failure paths

Two of the safe-failure checks above are hard to exercise against the real
sheets, so `tests/` covers them against a local HTTP fixture server instead
(`tests/fixture_server.py`) — no real sheet access or network needed:

- **Bad-status row with a valid amount** — a transaction with a non-blank,
  parseable `amount` but a `status` outside `posted`/`pending`/`disputed`
  must raise `SafeFailure`. The amount has to be non-blank: a blank/
  unparseable amount routes the row to `unknown_amount` *before* the status
  is ever checked, so a blank-amount version of the same bad status is
  included as a sanity check that must **not** raise.
- **Role-mismatch header** — a sheet whose header doesn't fingerprint to
  any of transactions/budget/revenue must raise `SafeFailure`. No special
  row is needed; the header alone decides this.

Run from `daily-financial-health-brief/`:

```
python3 -m unittest tests.test_untestable_paths -v
```

amounts and negative values are handled, and which decisions came directly
from the Finance and Operations Manager are in
[`references/business-rules.md`](references/business-rules.md).

(`tests/fixture_server.py`, no real sheet access or network needed) or as

  `posted`/`pending`/`disputed` must raise `SafeFailure`. The amount has to

  `unknown_amount` *before* the status is ever checked, so a blank-amount
  version of the same bad status is included as a sanity check that must

  header doesn't fingerprint to any of transactions/budget/revenue must
  raise `SafeFailure`. No special row is needed; the header alone decides
  this.
- **amount_status mismatch and orphan categories**
  (`test_amount_status_and_orphan_category.py`) — a transaction whose
  `amount_status` disagrees with whether `amount` actually parses must be
  excluded from both cash and MTD budget totals; a category with posted
  spend but no Budget Targets row must appear as an orphan, not silently
  vanish.

  missing `--comparison-date` must raise `SafeFailure` end-to-end; a
  comparison date with zero rows must be flagged, not failed; the signed
  change must be `target − comparison` in both directions.

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

input.content:
Add required --comparison-date and Daily Posted Total Comparison

The Leaderboard challenge requires daily posted totals and their signed
change against a comparison date (e.g. Aug 11 vs. Aug 10), which nothing in
the script implemented. Per the Work Sim interview, the Finance and
Operations Manager strictly uses the exact dates given in each request --
never an inferred one -- for financial consistency and alignment with the
review period. So:

- --comparison-date is a required, explicit CLI argument with no silent
  default. Missing it is a SafeFailure, same pattern as a missing source
  sheet: clear stderr message, exit 1, no deliverables written.
- build_posted_comparison() computes the signed change in Posted cash
  (target - comparison), reusing build_cash_summary()'s own validation so
  an unrecognized status on the comparison date still blocks the run.
- A comparison date with zero Transaction Ledger rows does not fail the
  run -- it doesn't corrupt any other figure in the report, so it's
  flagged "no comparison data available" in the new Daily Posted Total
  Comparison report section instead.

Regenerates deliverables/ with --target-date 2026-08-11
--comparison-date 2026-08-10 (the example from the challenge description)
so the committed deliverable reflects the new section.

def build_posted_comparison(
    all_transactions: list[dict],
    target_posted_total: Decimal,
    comparison_date: dt.date,
) -> dict:
    """Signed change in Posted cash between --target-date and the required,
    explicit --comparison-date (see build_cash_summary for why an
    unrecognized status on either date still blocks the run). A comparison
    date with zero Transaction Ledger rows doesn't corrupt anything else in
    the report, so it's flagged rather than failing the run."""
    comparison_str = comparison_date.isoformat()
    comparison_day_transactions = [t for t in all_transactions if t["date"] == comparison_str]

    comparison_available = bool(comparison_day_transactions)
    comparison_total = None
    signed_change = None
    if comparison_available:
        comparison_summary = build_cash_summary(comparison_day_transactions)
        comparison_total = comparison_summary["totals"]["posted"]
        signed_change = target_posted_total - comparison_total

    return {
        "comparison_date": comparison_date,
        "comparison_available": comparison_available,
        "comparison_total": comparison_total,
        "signed_change": signed_change,
    }

def most_recent_revenue_observation(
    revenue_rows: list[dict], metric: str, as_of_date: dt.date
) -> tuple[dt.date, Decimal] | None:
    """The most recent real Revenue Snapshot value for `metric` on or before
    as_of_date. The Revenue Snapshot updates sparsely by design -- it does
    not get a row for every day the way the Transaction Ledger does -- so
    falling back to the most recent real observation, clearly labeled with
    its own date, is not the same as assuming zero for an unknown amount:
    one is a real (if slightly stale) number, the other has no factual
    basis at all. Returns None if there's no observation at or before
    as_of_date (e.g. the date predates the Revenue Snapshot's first row)."""
    as_of_str = as_of_date.isoformat()
    candidates = [
        (row["date"], parse_amount(row["value"]))
        for row in revenue_rows
        if row["metric"] == metric and row["date"] <= as_of_str
    ]
    candidates = [(date_str, value) for date_str, value in candidates if value is not None]
    if not candidates:
        return None
    best_date_str, best_value = max(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])
    return dt.date.fromisoformat(best_date_str), best_value


def build_revenue_comparison(
    revenue_rows: list[dict], target_date: dt.date, comparison_date: dt.date
) -> dict:
    """Two independent as-of comparisons -- collected_revenue and
    outstanding_balance -- each target-date vs. comparison-date, exactly
    like build_posted_comparison() but for the Revenue Snapshot. These are
    never combined into a single relationship or ratio between the two
    metrics; each is reported on its own."""
    result = {}
    for metric in REVENUE_COMPARISON_METRICS:
        target_obs = most_recent_revenue_observation(revenue_rows, metric, target_date)
        comparison_obs = most_recent_revenue_observation(revenue_rows, metric, comparison_date)
        signed_change = (
            target_obs[1] - comparison_obs[1] if target_obs and comparison_obs else None
        )
        result[metric] = {
            "target_as_of": target_obs[0] if target_obs else None,
            "target_value": target_obs[1] if target_obs else None,
            "comparison_as_of": comparison_obs[0] if comparison_obs else None,
            "comparison_value": comparison_obs[1] if comparison_obs else None,
            "signed_change": signed_change,
        }
    return result
